notes.1: (a) Well attempted. Many candidates understood that a financial bonus involved an extra payment for good performance. Better candidates were able to give a precise definition. A common mistake was to say why it was used which did not explain the term. Others stated it represented extra money without explaining what it was for. ( b) Well answered by most candidates. (c) This question proved challenging for most candidates. Those who did well were able to identify at least one method with praise and promotion being typical choices. Only the best responses linked points to this business. The common mistake was to identify hygiene factors which do not act as motivators. 0450 Business Studies June 2016 (d) Generally well attempted. Most were able to identify at least one problem. Better candidates developed points such as ‘cost of equipment’ and ‘need for retraining’ to show how they could hinder a business. There were two common mistakes. Instead of development, some candidates identified a different knowledge point or stated that a certain issue would be problem without saying how it would impact on the business. Many candidates did not link answers to the scenario. (e) Good knowledge of issues was evident in most responses. Better answers attempted to consider the possible benefits (or not) of using efficiency as a way to improve profits. The best answers made good use of the information provided to help support their final decision. A large number of responses identified simple points such as less wastage but were not able to develop the points. Evaluation in most responses was simple or not attempted.
notes.2: (a) Well defined by most candidates. (b) This question was generally well answered. The most common mistake was to omit the units. (c) Most candidates were able to identify at least one relevant benefit with increased retained profit and higher demand being common choices. The best responses were then able to link their answers to the scenario to show how it would help KC’s business. (d) Most responses identified relevant factors. Better responses developed the points such as available land or proximity to suppliers to show why these issues needed to be considered. The strongest answers used the information well and related it to this business. A common error was to use the same analysis point for both factors, credit can only be given for the same point once. (e) Good responses idenitfied and explained at least one point either for or against multinationals to show how or why this might affect individuals or businesses in country Y. These responses demonstrated good use of the source material to support points made and a judgement was then attempted. Weaker responses offered simple statements, which were not developed. Evaluation in many responses was simple or not attempted. Many responses discussed the possible impact on KC which was not the question asked.
notes.3: (a) A number of responses showed imprecise definitions of this term not gaining full credit. There were two common mistakes. Some repeated the words used in the question without explaining what an asset was. Others defined the term with fixed costs. (b) This question produced a range of responses. Many correctly calculated the current ratio. Some responses included the formula, but gave the wrong answer, so could still gain some credit. A number of candidates did not attempt this question. (c) Most candidates could identify at least one way. Candidates who did well were then able to show how points such as check business performance and help make investment decisions would help JT’s shareholders. Weaker answers ignored the context so offered general points that could be related to any business. (d) This question proved challenging for most candidates. Good responses identified at least one way and then showed how cutting the number of shops or workers might help reduce costs. Only the best answers applied their answers to JT by making good use of the source material provided. A large number of responses discussed ways in which the business could increase sales or profits which did not answer the question asked. (e) Good knowledge of issues including the impact of changing prices and variety was evident in many answers. Better responses developed their points to show how or why such factors might affect customers. The best answers then offered an appropriate decision based on points made. Weaker answers were characterised by simple statements that were not developed. Many responses did not make a justified conclusion as the evaluation was often a repeat of an earlier point or an unsupported statement. 0450 Business Studies June 2016
notes.4: (a) Generally well attempted by most candidates. Better candidates were able to offer a precise definition. (b) Most candidates understood that market research involved collecting information about customers or the market. Better candidates were able to provide a precise definition. (c) Most candidates could identify at least one reason with building reputation and gaining repeat customers being popular answers. Application in many responses was limited as candidates offered theoretical explanations, which would apply to any business. (d) Most candidates were able to identify and explain at least one benefit to a business of using social networks for promotion. The best answers made good use of the context to show the possible implications for this small phone repair company. Weaker responses did not develop the points made and repeated the knowledge point rather than offer any explanation. Application in many responses was limited. (e) Only the best responses included a fully supported evaluation. Such answers tried to discuss both advantages and disadvantages of becoming a franchisee. The best answers used the information provided in the stem to help them reach their decisions. A large number of candidates identified a number of simple points such as loss of control or help with marketing but offered no development. Evaluation in many responses was simple or not attempted. 0450 Business Studies June 2016 BUSINESS STUDIES
